title: Hardcoded API key or secret
why: A secret written directly into source code gets committed to version control and can leak publicly (e.g. via a public GitHub repo), letting anyone use your API credits or access your accounts.
fix: Load secrets from environment variables (os.environ) or a secrets manager, never write them directly in code.

title: Hardcoded AWS access key
why: AWS access keys found in code (especially public repos) are one of the most common causes of cloud account takeovers and surprise billing.
fix: Use environment variables or an IAM role instead of embedding AWS keys in code.

title: Use of eval()
why: eval() runs whatever string is passed to it as code. If any part of that string comes from user input, an attacker can run arbitrary code on your server or app.
fix: Avoid eval() entirely. Use ast.literal_eval() for safely parsing data, or a proper parser/dispatch table for logic.

title: Use of exec()
why: Like eval(), exec() runs arbitrary code from a string. This is a common way AI-generated code accidentally creates a remote code execution vulnerability.
fix: Avoid exec(). Restructure the logic to not require running dynamically generated code.

title: subprocess call with shell=True
why: When shell=True is combined with any user-controlled input, an attacker can inject extra shell commands (shell injection) and run anything on the host machine.
fix: Use shell=False (the default) and pass command arguments as a list, e.g. subprocess.run(['ls', path]).

title: Possible SQL injection via string building
why: Building SQL queries by concatenating or f-string-formatting variables directly into the query lets an attacker inject their own SQL and read or modify data they shouldn't have access to.
fix: Use parameterized queries (e.g. cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?', (user_id,))) instead of building the query string manually.

title: Use of pickle for deserialization
why: Unpickling data from an untrusted source can execute arbitrary code — pickle is not a safe format for data you don't fully control.
fix: Use a safe format like JSON for data interchange, or validate the source is fully trusted before unpickling.

title: Debug mode enabled
why: Leaving debug mode on in a deployed app (e.g. Flask/Django) can expose stack traces, source code, and internal environment details to anyone who triggers an error.
fix: Ensure debug is set to False (or driven by an environment variable that defaults to False) before deploying.

title: Wildcard CORS policy
why: Allowing any website (*) to make authenticated requests to your API can let a malicious site read data on behalf of your logged-in users.
fix: Restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to a specific list of trusted domains.

title: Weak hashing algorithm (MD5/SHA1)
why: MD5 and SHA1 are broken for security purposes (collisions are practical to generate) and should not be used for passwords or integrity checks.
fix: Use bcrypt/argon2 for passwords, and SHA-256 or better for integrity/checksum purposes.
